description: MLR 2017 requires reporting under POCA s.330 when ML suspected
MLR 2017 requires reporting under TA s.19 when TF suspected
FCA SYSC 6.3 implements and elaborates on MLR 2017 obligations for FCA-authorised firms
FCA FCG provides non-binding guidance elaborating SYSC 6.3 requirements
JMLSG Guidance is HM Treasury-approved industry guidance under MLR 2017 reg.86
FCA publishes and updates the Financial Crime Guide
FCA enforces SYSC 6.3 financial crime requirements
UKFIU receives and processes all UK SARs
OFSI enforces financial sanctions under SAMLA 2018 SIs
MLRO is responsible for deciding to submit external SARs to the UKFIU
The MLRO SMF17 function is governed by SM&CR
CDD requires identification of beneficial owners meeting ≥25% threshold
EDD is mandatory for PEPs and family members/close associates
Filing of a SAR creates tipping-off restrictions under POCA s.333A
A SAR with consent request triggers the POCA s.338 authorised disclosure / consent regime
Post-Brexit, UK domestic PEPs treated at lower risk than EU AMLR Art.21 default
UK SAR regime (POCA/TA) diverges from EU AMLR STR regime — different thresholds and processes
Brexit created independent UK sanctions regime (SAMLA/OFSI) distinct from EU sanctions
ECCTA 2023 strengthens Companies House BO transparency and PSC register accuracy
ECTE Act 2022 expanded OFSI civil penalty powers and introduced monetary penalty regime
UK Wire Transfer Regulations 2017 remain in force; EU has updated to TFR 2023/1113 — UK divergence
FCA Dear CEO letters on AML issued by FCA supervision
UK NRA sector risk ratings inform the risk-based approach to CDD for individual firms
UK cryptoasset firms registered for AML under MLR 2017 are supervised by FCA
HMRC is the AML supervisor for MSBs not FCA-authorised
MLR 2017 reg.21 requires appointment of a nominated officer (MLRO)
SM&CR is an FCA/PRA regulatory framework
UWOs created under POCA as amended by ECTE Act 2022
High-risk third country EDD is triggered by UK-specific high-risk country list (informed by NRA)
